proposed.title: Spider-Man (1994)#23
proposed.text: Feeling pushed aside by Peter, Mary Jane turns to Harry and starts seeing him.
proposed.on_a_card_about_b: The woman Peter loves, who turns to Harry.
proposed.on_b_card_about_a: The man Mary Jane loves, though his secrets push her away.

changes.evidence: Mary Jane goes to Harry for comfort and starts a relationship with him when Morbius disappears and Peter comforts Felicia (end of The Immortal Vampire, #23; the Harry connection already puts this at #23). The current #41 stage compresses this break into the night she is kidnapped.

proposed.title: Spider-Man (1994)#35
proposed.text: After Spider-Man saves her from the Kingpin, Mary Jane gives back Harry's engagement ring, knowing she loves Peter.

changes.evidence: In The Ultimate Slayer (#35) Mary Jane, engaged to Harry, is kidnapped with Harry and Norman; after Spider-Man saves them she hands Harry back his ring and tells Spider-Man she does not love Harry and loves someone else. The reconciliation happens here, not in #41.

now.title: Spider-Man (1994)#41
now.text: When his secret life keeps him away, she leaves him for Harry, but she calls off their engagement because she still loves Peter. Then the Green Goblin kidnaps her, and she vanishes into a portal during his fight with Spider-Man.
now.on_a_card_about_b: The woman Peter loves, lost in a portal.
now.on_b_card_about_a: The man Mary Jane loves, though his secrets push her away.

proposed.text: Peter and Mary Jane are finally together when the Green Goblin kidnaps her, and she vanishes into a portal during his fight with Spider-Man.

changes.evidence: By Turning Point (#41) Mary Jane has already left Harry and is with Peter (Liz remarks they finally got together). Her turn to Harry (#23) and the broken engagement (#35) happen earlier; with the two added stages above the #41 text should hold only the kidnapping.

proposed.title: Spider-Man (1994)#41
proposed.text: Hurt that Mary Jane left him for Peter, Harry believes Peter betrayed him and wants nothing more to do with him.
proposed.on_a_card_about_b: Peter's old friend, who resents him over Mary Jane.
proposed.on_b_card_about_a: Harry's old friend, whom he blames for taking Mary Jane.

changes.evidence: In Turning Point (#41) Mary Jane says Harry thinks Peter betrayed him; Harry is cold to Peter at his birthday party, and by the end Harry wants nothing to do with Peter. A clear falling-out between the #35 and #49 stages.

proposed.title: Spider-Man (1994)#45
proposed.text: With Mary Jane and Norman both gone, Harry and Peter make up and become roommates again.
proposed.on_a_card_about_b: Peter's friend and roommate, Norman Osborn's son.

changes.evidence: At the end of The Return of Kraven (#45) Peter and Harry decide to share a flat again to help each other through their losses, a reconciliation before Harry turns Goblin in #49.

now.title: Spider-Man (1994)#53
now.text: Harry is sent to Ravencroft, then returns as the Goblin to attack Peter's wedding to Mary Jane, until Liz Allan talks him down.
now.on_a_card_about_b: Peter's friend, now the Green Goblin, out to kill him.
now.on_b_card_about_a: The hero Harry blames for his own father's loss.

proposed.on_a_card_about_b: Peter's friend, who turned Green Goblin and gives up his revenge.

changes.evidence: In The Wedding (#53) Liz Allan talks Harry down and he gives up his revenge and returns to Ravencroft, so the card's 'out to kill him' is no longer true from this stage on.

proposed.title: Spider-Man (1994)#53
proposed.text: Fisk pays for Peter's wedding to thank him for once saving his life, and Peter accepts though he knows Fisk is the Kingpin.
proposed.on_a_card_about_b: The crime lord behind most of Peter's troubles.
proposed.on_b_card_about_a: The hero who keeps ruining Fisk's plans.

changes.evidence: In The Wedding (#53) Peter visits Wilson Fisk, who offers to pay for his wedding because Peter saved his life from the Hobgoblin; despite knowing Fisk is the Kingpin, Peter accepts, and Fisk later sends the Mega-Slayer against the villains crashing the ceremony.

proposed.title: Spider-Man (1994)#45
proposed.text: The serum that changed Kraven turns Mariah into a feral creature, and Spider-Man helps bring her the cure that partly restores her.
proposed.on_a_card_about_b: A scientist who helps cure Peter.
proposed.on_b_card_about_a: Helps Mariah cure Kraven, then her.

changes.evidence: In The Return of Kraven (#45) the stalker is Mariah, mutated by the same serum Kraven gave her to save her life; Spider-Man, the Black Cat and Kraven give her Connors's serum, which partly reverses the change.

now.title: Spider-Man (1994)#44
now.text: Landon recreates the super soldier serum that turns Felicia into the Black Cat.
now.on_b_card_about_a: A hero who foils Landon's work.

proposed.title: Spider-Man (1994)#47
proposed.text: Landon has the Shocker seize Morbius so he can study him, until Spider-Man and the Black Cat break in and Morbius drains Landon's plasma.

changes.evidence: In The Black Cat (#44) Landon recreates the serum used on Felicia, but nothing passes between him and Spider-Man; in The Awakening (#47) Landon and the Shocker take Morbius, Spider-Man and the Black Cat interrupt, and Morbius drains Landon.

owner_calls.question: The X-Men '97#10 stage sorts first, before the blind date in Spider-Man (1994)#3, but it takes place after Madame Web takes Peter to find Mary Jane at the end of Spider-Man (1994)#65. Keep it where the universe order puts it, or move X-Men '97 after Spider-Man (1994) for this pair?
options: Order X-Men '97 S1 after Spider-Man (1994) in the Spider-Verse, so this becomes the last stage
owner_calls.evidence: Spider-Man (1994)#65 ends with Madame Web taking Spider-Man to find Mary Jane; X-Men '97 'Tolerance Is Extinction, Part 3' shows Peter, Mary Jane and Flash watching Asteroid M fall, i.e. he found her. Also, the same placement makes X-Men '97 S1 show up 'before the first stage' for Iron Man.
